rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: A landlord may only evict a residential tenant for one of the specific statutory good-cause reasons (such as nonpayment of rent, disorderly conduct, property damage, lease violations, or removal from the rental market), and in most cases must first serve a required notice (Notice to Cease and/or Notice to Quit) before filing suit.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; notice periods range from 3 days to 3 months depending on cause
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes and land in a mobile home park, apartment buildings and complexes, and rooming and boarding homes.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units; does not apply to hotel, motel, or guest house occupants who are transient or seasonal guests (unless they have no alternate residence and reside there continually); does not apply to a unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled immediate family member who permanently occupies the unit.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord must have good cause to evict a tenant (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-53).

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether a unit is held in trust for and permanently occupied by a developmentally disabled immediate family member, or is used for transient/seasonal hotel, motel, or guest house occupancy
